svg.title: Rolling-boil water treatment in three stages
svg.desc: Working three-stage Victorian field-water diagram. First reject salt or brackish water, algae or scum, floodwater, a current warning, sewage, mine, farm or industrial runoff, fuel, ash or firefighting chemicals. No visible warning does not prove safety. Second, use a suitable unsealed heat-safe pot and only a lawful heat source that can be operated exactly as instructed; bring the whole water surface to a vigorous rolling boil, then turn off the heat as instructed. Third, cool the pot on a stable non-combustible heat-safe surface protected from new contamination. Use promptly when cool enough, or pour into a clean closed drinking-water container without touching its inside or opening. Boiling treats most microbial hazards, not salt, algal toxins, chemicals or metals. The rolling-boil principle has an editorial source-match estimate of ninety-five per cent and the field handling sequence eighty per cent; these are not safety probabilities.
